title: Signal Contrivance Catalogue: compact synthesis of runtime feedback & feature asks
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc compiles a compact, prioritized synthesis of recent runtime-related customer feedback (Aug–Oct 2026) and translates those signals into candidate low/med/high-effort fixes, probes, and product asks for ENG, PLM, and SRE. Aim is to surface high-impact runtime friction that disproportionately affects mid-market customers using Dedicated and Private deployments, and to propose narrow experiments that can reduce support load and token-cost regressions.

How this was assembled:
- Source streams: customer support transcripts, onboarding calls (x6), dedicated customer runbooks, field notes from Solutions Eng, and 12 CS tickets flagged as "runtime-urgent".
- Timestamps span 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-10.
- Lean clustering applied: latency & tail spikes, kv-cache misses, model fallback noise, quota/route mismatch.

Topline synthesis (one-liner):
Operational unpredictability — sudden tail-latency spikes and cache-miss patterns — drives workaround engineering and contract churn. Customers want clearer SLO signals and cheap mitigations (auto-warm, cache diagnostics, safer fallbacks) rather than large re-architectures.

Representative customer vignettes (anonymized):
- "During peak batch, our response times doubled for a few hours — our UI timed out and we lost customers." (mid-market fintech, Dedicated)
- "After a model roll we saw higher hallucination rates plus cost increase — we suspect quantized variant routing was engaged unexpectedly." (AI-native search startup, Hosted with Dedicated fallback)
- "Our on-prem instance showed repeated KV-cache cold starts after brief network flaps — warmups helped but heat was manual and error-prone." (enterprise regulated customer, Private)

Signal clusters and impact notes:
1) KV-cache cold start patterns (HIGH frequency, HIGH pain for Private + Dedicated)
- Symptom: burst of requests after idle window -> first N tokens experience high latency, increased tail.
- Evidence: logs from three customers show repeated LRU evictions correlated with autoscaler cycles and infrequent long-running prompts.
- Customer impact: UI timeouts, perception of instability; manual workarounds include explicit warmup calls and conservatively increasing idle retention (costly).

2) Unsafe fallback variants and quality regressions (MED frequency, HIGH severity)
- Symptom: automatic fallback to quantized or smaller variants when capacity tight, with no observable trace in Console for customers, and no configurable guardrails.
- Evidence: CS ticket RD-4821 + Slack thread where model_id changed mid-session causing mismatched outputs.
- Customer impact: regression in product UX, lost trust; escalations to account teams.

3) Tail latency spikes correlated with batch-size heuristics (MED frequency, MED pain)
- Symptom: sudden queueing and long tail when workload mix shifts (short interactive requests interspersed with long async workloads).
- Evidence: trace slices show batching algorithm expanding window during burst; customers unable to tune batching without deep runtime access.
- Customer impact: degraded interactivity, ad-hoc workarounds (throttling client-side).

4) Cost stealth from implicit retries and opaque per-route configs (LOW frequency, MED pain)
- Symptom: customers see cost increase but cannot map to a particular route or retry policy; retries triggered by transient errors or model fallbacks.
- Evidence: cost breakdowns with token-level spikes aligned to retry windows; lack of per-route retry logs in Console.

Candidate fixes and probes (organized by estimated effort):
Low-effort (1–2 sprints / quick ops):
- Auto-warm endpoint: lightweight warmup request pattern that can be enabled per-deployment; 1–2 small calls post-idle to prefetch KV entries. Risks: small added baseline cost; needs opt-in default.
- Cache-diagnostics endpoint/metric: expose recent eviction counters and estimated cold-start risk per node in Console + API. This is high-visibility and helps CS triage.
- Fallback transparency flag: when enabled, annotate responses with model-variant metadata and fallback reason headers (for debugging). Minimal instrumentation.

Medium-effort (2–6 sprints):
- Adaptive idle retention policy: runtime policy that prolongs KV retention selectively for tenants with bursty patterns (learned window). Requires safe heuristics and cost guardrails.
- Smart batching profiles per-route: allow customers to choose a "fast-interactive" profile vs "throughput-batched" profile that adjusts batching window and prioritization. Expose in Console.
- Retry/Backoff surfacing in Console: per-route retry counts and causes with simple alerting.

High-effort (>6 sprints):
- Predictive model-variant routing: precompute fallback compatibility and warm candidate variants to reduce quality regression windows during failover. Complex and longer lead time.
- Per-tenant token-cost simulator in Console: estimate cost impact of idle retention and warmups to decide on tradeoffs. Big UI + backend work.

Prioritization rubric (proposed):
- Customer pain (severity * number of affected customers) — weight 40%
- Support/operational load reduction — weight 30%
- Implementation complexity and risk — weight 20% (lower = higher priority)
- Revenue/contract risk — weight 10%
Applying rough scoring across the cluster, top candidates: 1) Cache-diagnostics endpoint (low effort, high CS ROI), 2) Fallback transparency flag (low effort, high trust recovery), 3) Adaptive idle retention pilot for 2 customers (medium effort, high impact).

Quick experiment proposals (minimal viable probes):
- Two-week warmup A/B: enable auto-warm on 2 mid-market Dedicated customers and compare tail latency and cost delta. Instrument with eviction counters.
- Fallback metadata rollout: add model-variant headers for all Hosted responses in staging, ship to 5 customers as an opt-in. Track rollback incidents.
- Batching profile toggle: add a header to allow passing "fast-interactive" for a subset of requests from a partner to observe latency tradeoffs.

Open questions & unknowns:
- What are per-tenant billing/contract constraints for enabling warmups by default? Need billing & legal input.
- Is exposing eviction counters a security concern for multi-tenant clusters? Ask SRE/security.
- Could adaptive idle retention increase overall cluster memory pressure? Need infra capacity study.

Recommended next steps (owner suggestions):
- CS: run the two-week warmup A/B on 2 customers (owner: Aisha). Gather eviction/time-series and customer feedback. Start by 2026-11-01.
- ENG-serving-runtime: scope Cache-diagnostics API (owner: Jon Park). 2-sprint spike to deliver a read-only metrics endpoint and Console tile.
- PLM: draft fallback transparency flag UX and marketing copy for opt-in (owner: Miguel).
- SRE: quick review of security/billing implications for warmup and eviction metrics (owner: SRE on-call).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This doc purposefully blends CS signal with narrow engineering asks — treat as a probe-first backlog rather than a launch plan.
- If prioritized, prefer doing the low-effort diagnostics + transparency work first to give customers immediate insight and reduce noise before larger changes.

Appendix: raw cue checklist (for CS handoff)
- Pull logs: eviction counters, autoscaler events, model-variant switches for the last 72 hours for affected tenant.
- Customer-facing FAQ draft: short note explaining warmup opt-in, approximate cost impact, and how to opt-out.
- Short survey: 3 questions to send to pilot customers after warmup A/B (perceived latency change, willingness to accept small cost, any false positives).

End.
